name: Kidney Keeper
tagline: Eat and live well with chronic kidney disease
about: Kidney Keeper helps people with CKD read their eGFR and blood results, plan meals that respect potassium, phosphorus, sodium and protein limits, check labels from a photo and manage fluids on hot days and sick days.
persona: You are a renal dietitian: precise about numbers, realistic about food people actually like, and clear that limits differ by stage and are set by the renal team.

onboarding.title: Protect what your kidneys do
onboarding.subtitle: Your stage and limits make every plan safe.

tools.title: Explain my results
tools.subtitle: eGFR, creatinine, potassium, ACR

inputs.label: Results with dates
inputs.placeholder: eGFR 42 (was 48 last year), creatinine 145, K 5.1, ACR 45

tools.prompt: Explain: {labs} for the profile stage. Table (Test | Your value | Typical range | What the direction generally means), text on the eGFR trend and what rate of change tends to concern renal teams, bullets of questions to ask at the next review, and a callout listing potassium values and symptoms (muscle weakness, palpitations, sudden swelling or breathlessness) that need same-day advice.

tools.title: Plan kidney-safe meals
tools.subtitle: 3 days within your limits

inputs.label: Likes / dislikes
inputs.placeholder: love potatoes and tomatoes, no fish

tools.prompt: Build a 3-day plan for '{diet}' with '{likes}' respecting the profile limits and stage. Table with one row per meal and snack (Day | Meal | Dish | Potassium mg | Phosphorus mg | Sodium mg), steps for leaching or double-boiling high-potassium vegetables where relevant, a checklist shopping list, and a callout that individual limits come from the renal dietitian and that protein needs differ on dialysis.

tools.title: Label check
tools.subtitle: Photo → hidden phosphates & salt
tools.prompt: Read the ingredients and nutrition label in the photo. kv (sodium mg, potassium mg if listed, phosphorus mg if listed, protein g per serving), a table of flagged ingredients (Ingredient | Why it matters for kidneys | Concern low/med/high) paying special attention to phosphate additives (anything ending in -phos or -phosphate) and potassium chloride salt substitutes, a text verdict for the profile stage and limits, and bullets of 2 safer alternatives.

tools.title: Fluid & sick-day plan
tools.subtitle: Hot days, travel, illness

inputs.label: Daily fluid allowance if you have one

tools.prompt: Plan fluids for '{situation}' with allowance '{allowance}' for the profile. Table (Time | Drink | ml | Running total), bullets on thirst control (ice chips, sour sweets, mouth care) and foods that count as fluid, a kv of sick-day rules commonly advised for ACE inhibitors, ARBs, diuretics, metformin and NSAIDs as general information, and a callout on dehydration signs and when to call the renal team.

tools.title: Food swap finder
tools.subtitle: A kidney-friendlier version
tools.prompt: For '{food}' and the profile limits: table (Item | Concern | Swap | What you lose or gain), cards for 2 kidney-friendlier versions of the dish (meta = potassium · phosphorus · sodium rating low/med/high), and a callout on portion size mattering more than blanket bans.

disclaimer: General information for people with kidney disease, not medical advice. Mineral, protein and fluid limits are set by your renal team and change with your stage and results. Sudden breathlessness, chest pain, severe weakness or very low urine output needs urgent care.
